notes: A very wide Greek word: a spoken word, a message, an account, and also the reason or order behind things. In John 1 the Word is a person who was with God and was God, through whom everything was made, and who became flesh. John uses the word in the Jewish sense of God's creating word (Genesis 1) and God's wisdom, and in the Greek sense of the ordering reason of the world.

elsewhere.note: The seed is the word of God.
The Word of life.
The word of God is living and active.
His name is called The Word of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to pitch a tent, to dwell
notes: Literally "to live in a tent," from the word for tent or tabernacle. John 1:14 says the Word "lived among us" using this verb, which recalls the tabernacle in the wilderness where God's glory dwelt. It appears in the New Testament mostly in John and Revelation.

elsewhere.note: He who sits on the throne will spread his tent over them.
The dwelling of God is with man.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Literally "one of a kind," and by extension an only child. Luke uses it for the only son of the widow of Nain, Jairus' only daughter, and the only child of a father (Luke 7:12, 8:42, 9:38). John uses it of Jesus as the unique Son (1:14, 1:18, 3:16, 3:18). It may emphasize uniqueness more than birth, which is why some translations read "one and only."

elsewhere.note: The only son of his mother.
His only daughter.
Abraham offered his only son.
God sent his only Son into the world.

uncertain: Whether monogenēs emphasizes "only born" or "one of a kind" is debated, which is why translations differ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Light, and by extension what makes things visible and what exposes. In John, light and darkness are central: the Word is the light of men (1:4-9), Jesus says "I am the light of the world" (8:12), and those who do evil hate the light (3:19-21).

elsewhere.note: You are the light of the world.
A light for revelation to the Gentiles.
The light of the knowledge of the glory of God.
God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A lamb. John the Baptist calls Jesus "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" (1:29, 1:36). It may recall the Passover lamb, the lamb of Isaiah 53, or the daily temple offering; which is meant is debated.

elsewhere.note: As a lamb before its shearer is silent.
The precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb.

uncertain: Which Old Testament lamb John the Baptist has in mind is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To give evidence as a witness. It is one of John's most important words: John the Baptist testifies (1:7, 1:15, 1:32, 1:34), the Father testifies, the works testify, and at the end the disciple who wrote testifies (21:24). The word gives us "martyr."

elsewhere.note: All spoke well of him.
To him all the prophets bear witness.
Demetrius has received a good testimony from everyone.
He who testifies to these things says, Surely I am coming soon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Life, especially the life that comes from God. John uses it far more than any other Gospel: "In him was life" (1:4), and he wrote "that believing you may have life in his name" (20:31). It is usually joined with "eternal" (aionios) for life of the age to come that begins now.

range.note: Life of the age to come.

elsewhere.note: The way is narrow that leads to life.
One's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions.
The free gift of God is eternal life.
Whoever has the Son has life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Truth, reality, and faithfulness. In John, truth is a person's reliability and what is real as opposed to shadow: Jesus is "full of grace and truth" (1:14), says "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (14:6), and the Spirit is the "Spirit of truth" (14:17).

elsewhere.note: She told him the whole truth.
They exchanged the truth about God for a lie.
Created after God in righteousness and holiness of truth.
The truth is not in us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To believe, trust, or put faith in. John uses the verb nearly a hundred times and never uses the noun "faith." He often says "believe in" Jesus, meaning to put one's trust in him, and says his whole book was written "that you may believe" (20:31).

elsewhere.note: Repent and believe in the gospel.
Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved.
If you believe in your heart that God raised him.
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A word that can mean "from above," "from the beginning," or "again." Jesus tells Nicodemus that one must be born "anothen" (3:3, 3:7), and Nicodemus hears "again," while Jesus also means "from above" (compare 3:31 and 19:11). John often uses double meanings like this.

elsewhere.note: The curtain was torn from top to bottom.
Every good gift is from above.
Do you want to be enslaved again?
Having followed everything closely from the first.

uncertain: Whether John 3:3 means "born again" or "born from above" (or both) is debated; the Greek word allows both.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To raise high. John uses it with a deliberate double meaning: Jesus will be "lifted up" on the cross (3:14, 8:28, 12:32-34) and thereby exalted. Elsewhere in the New Testament it means to exalt or honor, as in "whoever humbles himself will be exalted."

elsewhere.note: Whoever exalts himself will be humbled.
Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled.
Being exalted at the right hand of God.
Humble yourselves, that he may exalt you.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A judging, a decision, and by extension a verdict or time of judgment. It gives us "crisis." John says that the light has come, and "this is the judgment" that people chose darkness (3:19), and that the Father has given all judgment to the Son (5:22).

elsewhere.note: You have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy.
It is appointed for man to die once, and after that comes judgment.
The hour of his judgment has come.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Water. In John water carries layers of meaning: the water made wine (2:7-9), the water of birth and Spirit (3:5), "living water" for the woman at the well (4:10-14), and the water that flows from Jesus' side (19:34).

elsewhere.note: I baptize you with water.
I baptize you with water.
The washing of water with the word.
The water of life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A sign, a miracle that points beyond itself. John calls Jesus' miracles "signs" (2:11, 4:54, 6:14, 12:18) and says they were written down "that you may believe" (20:30-31).

range.note: Something that identifies, like a signal.
A wonder that points to God's work.
A sign of what is coming.

elsewhere.note: Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.
The Lord worked with them and confirmed the word by the signs.
Jesus of Nazareth, attested by God with signs.
A great sign appeared in heaven.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Splendor, honor, and the visible presence of God. John says "we saw his glory" (1:14), and at Cana Jesus "revealed his glory" (2:11).

elsewhere.note: They saw his glory.
All have fallen short of the glory of God.
The knowledge of the glory of God.
He is the radiance of God's glory.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Breath, wind, or spirit. Jesus plays on the double meaning in 3:8 ("the wind blows where it wants") and says "God is spirit" (4:24).

range.note: The Holy Spirit, or a spirit being.
Life, the breath of a person.

elsewhere.note: The Holy Spirit will come on you.
They were all filled with the Holy Spirit.
Those led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
The Spirit searches everything.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: eternal, of the age to come
notes: Eternal, of the age to come. For John it is the quality of life that comes through belief and begins now: "whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life" (3:15-16).
uncertain: How to understand "eternal punishment" (25:46), as endless or as belonging to the age to come, has been debated across church history.

elsewhere.note: What good thing shall I do to have eternal life?
What must I do to inherit eternal life?
The gift of God is eternal life.
God gave us eternal life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The verb of self-giving love. "God so loved the world" (3:16) uses it, and the Father loves the Son (3:35).

range.note: Care for another that shows itself in action.

elsewhere.note: Love your enemies.
Love your enemies.
Love is the fulfillment of the law.
We love because he first loved us.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To bow down, to worship. Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that true worshippers "will worship the Father in spirit and truth" (4:23-24).

range.note: Give God the honor due to him.

elsewhere.note: We came to worship him.
Worship the Lord your God.
They fall down before him who sits on the throne.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: One who saves. The Samaritans say "this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world" (4:42).

range.note: A royal or divine title in the Greek world.

elsewhere.note: A Savior, who is Christ the Lord.
God exalted him to be Leader and Savior.
We eagerly await a Savior.
Our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Healthy, sound, or whole. The man at the pool is asked, "Do you want to be made well (hygies)?" (5:6), and is later said to have been made "well" (5:9, 5:11, 5:14-15). It gives us "hygiene."

elsewhere.note: His hand was restored, healthy as the other.
The mute speaking, the crippled healthy.
This man is standing before you well.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A work or deed, what someone does. Jesus speaks of the Father's "work" and of his own "works" as evidence of who he is (5:17, 5:20, 5:36, 10:25, 14:10-12). In John the works are the signs and also the whole of what Jesus does for the Father.

elsewhere.note: Let them see your good works.
Created in Christ Jesus for good works.
Faith by itself, if it does not have works, is dead.
I am doing a work in your days.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to give life, to make alive
notes: From "life" and "to make." To bring to life, or to impart life. Jesus says the Father raises the dead and gives them life, and so does the Son (5:21), and that the Spirit gives life (6:63). Paul uses it of the resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:22).

elsewhere.note: God, who gives life to the dead.
In Christ shall all be made alive.
The last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
The Spirit gives life.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A writing, and in the New Testament most often the Scriptures, the books of the Old Testament. Jesus says, "You search the Scriptures ... they testify about me" (5:39). It is also used for a single passage ("the Scripture says").

elsewhere.note: He interpreted to them in all the Scriptures.
Examining the Scriptures daily.
All Scripture is breathed out by God.
No prophecy of Scripture comes from private interpretation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The bread-like food God provided to Israel in the wilderness (Exodus 16). The crowd mentions it to ask for a sign (6:31), and Jesus answers that it was not Moses who gave it, and that he himself is the true bread from heaven (6:32-35, 6:49-51).

elsewhere.note: The golden urn holding the manna.
To the one who conquers I will give some of the hidden manna.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Flesh, the physical body, and by extension human nature in its weakness. John 1:14 says the Word became flesh, and in chapter 6 Jesus says the bread he gives is his flesh (6:51-56), though he also says "the flesh profits nothing" (6:63), speaking of flesh without the Spirit. Paul uses it more negatively, of human nature set against God.

elsewhere.note: Flesh and blood has not revealed this to you.
A spirit does not have flesh and bones.
God sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh.
Jesus Christ has come in the flesh.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To pull or drag, as of a net or a person. No one can come to Jesus unless the Father "draws" him (6:44), and Jesus says, "I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself" (12:32).

elsewhere.note: They were not able to haul it in.
They dragged Paul and Silas into the marketplace.
Is it not the rich who drag you into court?

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A religious festival, especially the great pilgrim feasts: Passover, Pentecost, and Booths. John organizes much of his Gospel around the feasts (2:13, 5:1, 6:4, 7:2, 10:22, 11:55), in which Jesus claims to fulfill what each celebrates.

elsewhere.note: At the feast the governor was accustomed to release a prisoner.
At every feast he used to release one prisoner.
His parents went every year to Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To thirst, literally and figuratively. John uses it for the woman at the well (4:14), for Jesus' offer in 6:35 and 7:37, and for Jesus' own cry on the cross, "I am thirsty" (19:28). The Beatitudes use it for those who "thirst for righteousness" (Matthew 5:6).

elsewhere.note: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness.
I was thirsty and you gave me drink.
If your enemy is thirsty, give him something to drink.
Let the one who is thirsty come.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To free a slave or prisoner. Jesus says the truth will make you free and, "If the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed" (8:32, 8:36). Paul uses it for freedom from sin (Romans 6:18, 6:22; 8:2).

elsewhere.note: Set free from sin.
The law of the Spirit has set you free.
For freedom Christ has set us free.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Sin, missing the mark. In John 8 Jesus says that everyone who commits sin is a bondservant of sin (8:34) and warns that unbelief means dying in one's sins (8:21, 8:24).

range.note: A wrong against God or others.

elsewhere.note: He will save his people from their sins.
The Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.
The wages of sin is death.
If we confess our sins.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A slave or bondservant. Jesus says "everyone who commits sin is the bondservant of sin" (8:34), and that a slave doesn't stay in the house forever, while a son does (8:35).

range.note: A title of honor for those who serve the Lord.

elsewhere.note: Whoever wishes to be first among you must be your slave.
You are slaves of the one whom you obey.
I would not be a servant of Christ.
Taking the form of a servant.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Bread, and by extension food. In John 6 it begins as barley loaves for the crowd and becomes the central image: "I am the bread of life" (6:35, 6:48).

elsewhere.note: Command that these stones become bread.
He broke the loaves.
He took bread, broke it, and gave it.
The Lord Jesus took bread.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To wake, raise up, rise. Jesus says "Arise, take up your mat" (5:8), and says the Father raises the dead and gives them life (5:21).

range.note: Lift or set on one's feet.

elsewhere.note: "He is risen, as he said."
"The Lord is risen indeed."
Believe that God raised him.
He was raised on the third day.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The devil, from a word meaning "slanderer." In 8:44 Jesus says to his opponents, "You are of your father, the devil," about those who want to kill him.

elsewhere.note: Jesus was led up to be tempted by the devil.
Tempted for forty days by the devil.
Stand against the schemes of the devil.
Resist the devil, and he will flee.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Blind, physically and also figuratively. John 9 is built on the contrast between a man blind from birth who comes to see and Pharisees who claim to see and are blind (9:39-41). Jesus also speaks of the "blind guides" (Matthew 15:14).

elsewhere.note: Two blind men followed him.
If the blind lead the blind, both will fall into a pit.
A blind man was sitting by the roadside begging.
You are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: "Away from the synagogue." It appears only in John (9:22, 12:42, 16:2): people who confess Jesus as the Christ are, or will be, expelled from the synagogue. The word reflects the pain of John's community, who lost their place in the Jewish community. How formal and how widespread the expulsion was is debated.
uncertain: How formal and widespread expulsion from the synagogue was, and whether it belongs to Jesus' day or to John's, is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A shepherd. In the Old Testament God is Israel's shepherd and kings and leaders are called shepherds. Jesus says "I am the good shepherd" (10:11, 10:14). The word is also used for a pastor in the church (Ephesians 4:11).

elsewhere.note: Like sheep without a shepherd.
Shepherds out in the field.
The great shepherd of the sheep.
The Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A door or gate. Jesus says "I am the door of the sheep" (10:7, 10:9), picking up the picture of a sheepfold with one entrance. Elsewhere in the New Testament it is used of the door to the kingdom (Luke 13:25) and of Christ standing at the door (Revelation 3:20).

elsewhere.note: Go into your room and shut the door.
The master has shut the door.
She came to answer the door.
I stand at the door and knock.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A voice or sound. In John 10 the sheep "hear his voice" and he calls them by name (10:3-5, 10:16, 10:27). The voice from heaven (12:28-30) and the voice that calls Lazarus out (11:43) use the same word.

elsewhere.note: A voice from heaven.
A voice came from heaven.
He heard a voice saying to him.
His voice was like the roar of many waters.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to be deeply moved, to snort with anger
notes: To snort like a horse, to be deeply agitated, to rebuke sternly. John uses it twice of Jesus at Lazarus' tomb (11:33, 11:38). The sense may be anger, deep distress, or both; why Jesus is moved this way is debated.

elsewhere.note: Jesus sternly warned them.
Sternly charging him, he sent him away.
They scolded her.

uncertain: Whether Jesus' reaction at the tomb is anger, grief, or both is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To sleep, and by extension to die, as a gentle way to describe death. Jesus says "Lazarus has fallen asleep" (11:11-13), and the disciples take it literally. In the New Testament believers who have died are said to have fallen asleep.

elsewhere.note: Many bodies of the saints who had fallen asleep were raised.
He fell asleep.
Some have fallen asleep.
Those who are asleep.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: An expensive perfume made from a plant that grew in the Himalayas. Mary pours a pound of pure nard on Jesus' feet (12:3), worth about three hundred denarii. The only other New Testament use is the similar account in Mark 14:3.

elsewhere.note: A woman with an alabaster flask of pure nard.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A grain or kernel of wheat or a mustard seed. Jesus says, "Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone. But if it dies, it bears much fruit" (12:24), in speaking of his coming death.

elsewhere.note: A grain of mustard seed.
It is like a grain of mustard seed.
It is like a grain of mustard seed.
A bare kernel, perhaps of wheat.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A ruler or leader. John uses it for Nicodemus, "a ruler of the Jews" (3:1), for the Jewish rulers who believed but wouldn't confess (12:42), and for "the ruler of this world" (12:31, 14:30, 16:11), meaning Satan.

elsewhere.note: A ruler came and knelt before him.
A ruler asked him.
The rulers were gathered together.
The prince of the power of the air.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Authority, the right and the power to act. Jesus says he has "power" (the same word) to lay down his life and to take it again (10:18).

range.note: Permission or freedom to do something.
The ability to make things happen.
Authority over others, or the people who hold it.

elsewhere.note: All authority has been given to me.
Governing authorities.
Delivered from the power of darkness.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Resurrection, "standing up again." Martha says her brother will rise "in the resurrection at the last day," and Jesus says "I am the resurrection and the life" (11:24-25).

elsewhere.note: Those who attain the resurrection from the dead.
Proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
How can some say there is no resurrection?
This is the first resurrection.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The council, the Jewish high court in Jerusalem. After Lazarus is raised, the chief priests and Pharisees "gather the council" (11:47).

elsewhere.note: The council seeks false witness.
The whole council looks for testimony.
The council of elders met.
The apostles are called before it.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: From a Hebrew cry in Psalm 118:25 meaning "save, please." The crowd shouts it as Jesus enters Jerusalem (12:13).

elsewhere.note: The same shout in Matthew.
The same shout in Mark.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: To wash a part of the body, especially hands and feet, as distinct from bathing the whole body. Jesus "began to wash the disciples' feet" (13:5-14). Mark 7:3 uses it of the Pharisees washing their hands before eating.

range.note: Clean a part of the body.

elsewhere.note: Wash your face.
Unless they wash their hands.
If she has washed the feet of the saints.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Something shown as a model, whether to follow or to avoid. Jesus says, "I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you" (13:15). It appears in Hebrews, James, and 2 Peter.

elsewhere.note: Fall by the same sort of disobedience.
A copy and shadow of the heavenly things.
An example of suffering and patience.
An example of what is going to happen to the ungodly.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: The end, in the sense of a goal or completion, not only a stopping point. John says Jesus "loved them to the end" (13:1), which can mean to the last moment, or to the fullest degree, or both. His last words on the cross, "It is finished," use a related verb (19:30).

elsewhere.note: The one who endures to the end will be saved.
Christ is the end of the law.
Then comes the end.
If we hold our confidence firm to the end.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: New in kind, fresh, as opposed to "new" in time (neos). The "new commandment" (13:34) is new in quality, because the standard is "as I have loved you." Other uses include the new covenant (Luke 22:20) and the new creation (2 Corinthians 5:17).

elsewhere.note: I will drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom.
The new covenant in my blood.
If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation.
A new heaven and a new earth.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A road or path, and by extension a way of life. Jesus says, "I am the way, the truth, and the life" (14:6). Early Christians were called followers of "the Way" (Acts 9:2). It is also the word used in quoting Isaiah 40:3, "prepare the way of the Lord."

elsewhere.note: The way is wide that leads to destruction.
Prepare the way of the Lord.
If he found any belonging to the Way.
The new and living way.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A place to stay, a lodging. Jesus says, "In my Father's house are many dwelling places" (14:2), and later, "We will come to him, and make our home with him" (14:23). The King James Version rendered it "mansions." These are the only two places in the New Testament where it appears.
uncertain: Whether the "dwelling places" of John 14:2 are in heaven, or refer to a relationship with the Father, or both, is debated.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: Someone called alongside to help: a counselor, advocate, comforter, or helper. John uses it only of the Holy Spirit, in the farewell discourse (14:16, 14:26, 15:26, 16:7). In 1 John 2:1, it is used of Jesus as an advocate with the Father. Translations vary: Helper, Counselor, Advocate, Comforter.

range.note: One who speaks on your behalf.

elsewhere.note: We have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to keep, to guard, to obey
notes: To keep, guard, or observe. In John it is the word for keeping Jesus' word and commandments (14:15, 14:21-24, 15:10), and Jesus also says he has kept those the Father gave him (17:12).

elsewhere.note: If you would enter life, keep the commandments.
Peter was kept in prison.
By this we know that we have come to know him, if we keep his commandments.
Blessed are those who keep what is written in it.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

notes: A grapevine. In the Old Testament, Israel is God's vine. Jesus says, "I am the true vine" (15:1, 15:5), meaning the faithful Israel in whom the branches live.

elsewhere.note: The fruit of the vine.
The fruit of the vine.
Gather the clusters from the vine of the earth.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

gloss: to remain, to abide, to stay
notes: To stay, remain, dwell. It is John's favorite word for relationship: remain in Jesus, as a branch in the vine (15:4-10), and let his word remain in you. In John 1:32-39 the Spirit remains on Jesus, and the disciples ask where he is "staying."

elsewhere.note: Stay with us, for it is toward evening.
He stayed with them and worked.
So now faith, hope, and love abide.
Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you.

Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline.

elsewhere.note: He found them sleeping for sorrow.
I have great sorrow and unceasing anguish.
Godly grief produces repentance.
Sorrow upon sorrow.

Overcome evil with good.
This is the victory that has overcome the world, our faith.
The one who conquers.

elsewhere.note: Glorify your Father who is in heaven.

Those he justified he also glorified.

I have not known a man.

We know the Spirit of truth.

elsewhere.note: You are the light of the world.

God chose what is foolish in the world.
Do not love the world.

elsewhere.note: The two shall become one flesh.

Pilate hands him over to be crucified.

"Peace to you."
We have peace with God.
The peace of God that surpasses understanding.

Tribulation produces perseverance.

They have come out of the great tribulation.

Joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace.
For the joy set before him he endured the cross.

In your hearts, honor Christ as Lord.

elsewhere.note: The whole cohort gathered around him.
The whole battalion.
Cornelius, a centurion of the Italian Cohort.
The tribune of the cohort.

elsewhere.note: The soldiers of the governor took Jesus into the Praetorium.
Inside the courtyard, that is, the Praetorium.
To be guarded in Herod's praetorium.
My imprisonment has become known throughout the whole imperial guard.

elsewhere.note: Where is he who has been born king of the Jews?
In the days of Herod, king of Judea.
Saying that there is another king, Jesus.
King of kings and Lord of lords.

notes: To love as a friend, to have affection for, to like, and also to kiss. In John 21:15-17 Jesus asks Peter "Do you love (agapaō) me?" twice, and then "Do you love (phileō) me?" while Peter always answers with phileō. Many scholars think the two verbs are interchangeable in John, but some read the shift as meaningful.

uncertain: Whether the change between agapaō and phileō in John 21 carries a meaning is debated; many scholars read them as synonyms.
